payload.markdown: So any class that extends an abstract class must implement all abstract methods or itself be declared abstract. An extending class is responsible for more than simply implementing an abstract method. In doing so, it must reproduce the method signature. This means that the access control of the implementing method cannot be stricter than that of the abstract method. The implementing method should also require the same number of arguments as the abstract method, reproducing any class type declarations.

items: Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Interfaces: A pure contract of method signatures with no implementation.
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Type Declarations: Parameter and return types that constrain what a function accepts and returns.

8203.title: Abstract Classes
8203.code:
<?php
abstract class ShopProductWriter
{
    protected array $products = [];

    public function addProduct(ShopProduct $shopProduct): void
    {
        $this->products[] = $shopProduct;
    }
}

    You can create methods and properties as normal, but any attempt to instantiate an
abstract object in this way will cause an error:

// listing 04.10
$writer = new ShopProductWriter();

<?php
abstract class ShopProductWriter
{
    protected array $products = [];

    public function addProduct(ShopProduct $shopProduct): void
    {
        $this->products[] = $shopProduct;
    }

    abstract public function write(): void;
}

8206.title: Here are two implementations of ShopProductWriter—first, XmlProductWriter
8206.code:
<?php
class XmlProductWriter extends ShopProductWriter
{

    public function write(): void
    {
        $writer = new \XMLWriter();
        $writer->openMemory();

        $writer->startDocument('1.0', 'UTF-8');
        $writer->startElement("products");
        foreach ($this->products as $shopProduct) {
            $writer->startElement("product");
            $writer->writeAttribute("title", $shopProduct->getTitle());
            $writer->startElement("summary");
            $writer->text($shopProduct->getSummaryLine());
            $writer->endElement(); // summary
            $writer->endElement(); // product
        }
        $writer->endElement(); // products
        $writer->endDocument();
        print $writer->flush();
    }
}

8207.title: This is the more basic TextProductWriter
8207.code:
<?php
class TextProductWriter extends ShopProductWriter
{
    public function write(): void
    {
        $str = "PRODUCTS:\n";
        foreach ($this->products as $shopProduct) {
            $str .= $shopProduct->getSummaryLine() . "\n";
        }
        print $str;
    }
}
